Carefree Pool Service for Pools Among the Boulders and Open Desert

Carefree buys and treats its water through its own town-owned water company, and many of its pools sit among native boulders and desert. Call the free line any hour to be put through to an independent, locally owned pool service company.

Carefree pool service has a few local twists. The town's water comes through its own water company, and many homes sit on natural desert lots where boulders and native plants run right up to the pool. Here is what that means for keeping a pool clean and its equipment running, and how to reach a nearby pool company with one free phone call.

Phoenix Pool Cleaning Pro does not service pools. When you dial (623) 240-0428, a short automated exchange covers what the pool is doing, and then the line hands the call to an independent, locally owned pool service company that works in Carefree. That company sees the pool, quotes its own price, does the work and is paid by you directly.

Carefree: a small desert town with a water company of its own

Carefree sits in the desert foothills north of Scottsdale, next door to Cave Creek. Its water is handled by the Carefree Water Company, the town's own water provider, rather than by a big city department.

The company does not treat most of its own surface water. The town's water fact sheets explain that it holds a Central Arizona Project allocation and has "treat and transport" agreements with Scottsdale and Cave Creek, so CAP water is treated by a neighboring system and delivered to Carefree. The same materials describe the local groundwater supply as limited, which is why the company leans mainly on CAP water.

Carefree pool service and repairs people ask about

Routine pool cleaning and maintenance covers the weekly basics. Pools beside natural boulders and native plants often need extra filter cleaning, and a pool that sat untended needs green pool cleanup. On the repair side, a pump, filter, heater or automation problem is pool equipment repair, and a pool losing more water than the sun can explain points to leak repair.

What Carefree's water setup means for a pool

  • The sourceMainly Colorado River water delivered by the CAP, treated by a neighboring system under the company's treat and transport agreements, with a limited local groundwater supply.
  • The providerThe Carefree Water Company, which serves the town.
  • The hardnessAsk the water company for its latest annual water quality report. Neighboring Cave Creek, also on CAP water, reported 12 to 15 grains per gallon in 2018.

For a pool, the details of who treats the water matter less than what is dissolved in it. CAP water is hard, and in the dry desert air a pool loses water to evaporation every day. Each top off brings in more calcium, which shows up as crust at the waterline and scale inside a heater or salt cell. A pool company that tests calcium hardness, pH and alkalinity together, and adjusts toward balance, keeps that buildup slow.

Pools among boulders and native desert

A natural desert yard is beautiful, and it changes the work. Three things a careful pool technician watches on a Carefree lot:

What falls in

Native trees drop leaves, flowers and seed pods, and wind carries dust and plant litter off the surrounding desert. Skimmer baskets and filters fill faster than in a walled yard with a lawn.

Where the rain runs

On a sloped lot, storm runoff can carry soil and gravel toward the pool. After a heavy rain, the water may need extra cleaning and a chemistry check.

Rock features

Waterfalls and boulder edges look natural, but every crevice is a place for algae and scale to start. They need brushing and a close look for leaks where rock meets plaster.

Leaving a Carefree pool for the summer

If you spend part of the year away, the pool keeps working without you. Heat, sun and the monsoon season, which the National Weather Service sets as June 15 to September 30, can turn a clear pool green in a short time when chlorine runs out or the pump stops. A neglected pool also becomes a mosquito breeding site, which Maricopa County's vector control program investigates. Before you leave:

  1. Set up service first. Arrange regular visits before you go, not after a neighbor calls about the water.
  2. Make access easy. Agree on how the company enters the yard and that gates are closed and latched after every visit.
  3. Agree on repairs. Decide what the company may fix without calling you and what needs your approval first, and get its prices in writing.
  4. Leave the timer right. Confirm the pump schedule and that the equipment area is clear of debris.
  5. Plan for storms. Ask what the company does after a dust storm or heavy rain while you are away.

Safety basics. Never mix pool chemicals with each other, and keep them stored apart, dry, shaded and away from children. If you smell gas near a pool heater, leave the area, do not touch switches or the heater, and from a safe distance call your gas utility's emergency number or 911. Keep children away from any pool that is unfenced, uncovered or too cloudy to see the bottom.

You never pay the line. See how the line works.

Check the license first. Arizona's Registrar of Contractors (ROC) licenses contractors, and its residential classifications include R-6, Swimming Pool Service and Repair. Repairs, equipment replacement and resurfacing generally call for a licensed contractor; whether a cleaning-only service needs a license is not spelled out, so ask the ROC if it matters to you. Ask the company for its ROC license number and look it up on the ROC contractor search (opens in a new tab) before work begins. The line does not check this for you.

Common questions

Who supplies the water in Carefree, AZ?

The Carefree Water Company. Town water materials describe Central Arizona Project water that neighboring systems treat and deliver under agreements with the company, plus a limited local groundwater supply.

How hard is the water in Carefree?

This page does not quote a figure, because the water company's current annual report was not available to confirm one. Ask the Carefree Water Company for its latest Consumer Confidence Report, which lists hardness. For context, neighboring Cave Creek, which also uses CAP water, reported 12 to 15 grains per gallon in its 2018 report, which is very hard. Have the pool company test your pool's calcium hardness directly.

Can I get Carefree pool service and repairs from one call?

Yes. Describe what you need, whether it is weekly cleaning or a pump, filter, heater or leak repair, and the call goes to an independent pool company that works in Carefree. For repairs, ask for its Arizona ROC license number and check it before work begins.

What should I do with my pool if I am away for the summer?

Arrange regular service before you leave, give the company a way into the yard, and agree on who handles problems while you are gone. A Carefree summer means intense sun and monsoon storms, and a pool left alone for weeks can turn green and start breeding mosquitoes.
